Study goals and suitability for each patient are discussed in detail with the clients prior to enrollment. Although clinical trial enrollment may not be the best option for all patients, in many cases, clinical trial participation provides the opportunity to receive novel, cutting-edge therapies free of charge or at a reduced cost and may facilitate treatment of pets where it would not otherwise be possible due to financial constraints or lack of other therapy options. Criteria for enrollment are outlined for each tumor type below. Please direct referrals or questions to the Oncology Clinical Trials Service at 573-882-7821. Current Trials and Studies Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BI705564) for Canine B‑Cell Lymphoma The University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center is enrolling dogs in a clinical trial evaluating an investigational oral Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) inhibitor— BI705564 —for the treatment of newly diagnosed B‑cell lymphoma. This exploratory, multicenter field study aims to assess both efficacy and safety of BTK inhibition in canine patients. Eligibility includes: Dogs >1 year old and 10–50 kg in body weight Naïve , untreated B‑cell lymphoma confirmed by cytology or histology with immunophenotyping (flow cytometry) At least two peripheral lymph nodes ≥2 cm in longest diameter WHO stage II, III, or IV B‑cell lymphoma Adequate organ function on bloodwork and urinalysis Performance score of 0–1 (normal to mildly decreased activity) and life expectancy ≥1 month Owner consent Key exclusions: T‑cell lymphoma or involvement of skin, GI tract, or nervous system Internal‑only disease (mediastinum, liver, spleen) without peripheral lymph node enlargement Prior lymphoma treatment (chemotherapy, Tanovea, Laverdia, radiation) or long‑term corticosteroids (>2 weeks) Hypercalcemia, MDR1 deficiency, pregnancy/lactation, or concurrent trial enrollment Study overview: Dogs will receive oral BI705564 once daily for 3 months (84 days) at 5 mg/kg , with possible dose escalation to 10 mg/kg in certain cases depe
